10:34 < Baal> PicoGUI is inside the kernel?
10:34 < Filip> that lastone should contain everything, including bootloader
10:34 < Filip> it's a kernel with embedded ramdisk, ramdisk contains  picoGUI
10:34 < Baal> Ok 
10:35 < Baal> Thank you very much :)
10:35 < Filip> there is also a kernel with working input (using the hardware buttons)
10:35 < Filip> but consol only, allows you to try the basic commands (uname, ls, ....)
10:36 < Baal> Where is it?

10:39 < Filip> give it a try, it's pretty cool
10:39 < Baal> Ok
10:40 < Filip> (don't forget to gunzip the vmlinux_input.gz , and an entry for it in de  cyacfg.txt config file)
10:41 < Baal> Ok
10:46 < Baal> image=vmlinux_input
10:46 < Baal> label=linux4be-input
10:46 < Baal> append=console=tty0 root=/dev/ram
10:47 < Baal> Is thi ok?
10:47 < Filip> no console= 
10:47 < Filip> in fact  you do not need the append  line, unless you want to work over (broken) serial
10:47 < Baal> I dont even have a serial cable :)
10:48 < Filip> this is min:
10:48 < Filip> mine:
10:48 < Filip> image=vmlinux_input
10:48 < Filip> label=input
10:48 < Filip> image=vmlinux
10:48 < Filip> label=linux
10:48 < Filip> image=vmlinux
10:48 < Filip> label=serial
10:48 < Filip> append=console=ttyS00,115200
10:49 < Filip> if you plan on using serial, watch out which version of the bootloader you're using (the older ones use 9600, the newest 115200 baud)

16:47 < Baalz> Of course

16:48 < Baalz> I will make a préconfigured tarball that they only have to uncompress on their CF and boot
16:48 < Filip> (maybe call it 'internal memory' , I tihnk that's the term casio always uses)
16:49 < Filip> and a big fat disclaimer ;-)
16:49 < Baalz> This is where I am now
16:49 < Baalz> :)

16:53 < Filip> perfect
17:11 < Baalz> What do you think about what I said for the rocket button?
17:13 < Baalz> Rocket + keypad would scroll in history and the keypad only for inputing characters
17:13 < Filip> this is current mapping:
17:13 < Filip>  
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt = no action (it is used to shift other btns actions) 
17:13 < Filip>  * ok = enter 
17:13 < Filip>  * esc = tab 
17:13 < Filip>  * pwr = ctrl + alt + delete 
17:13 < Filip>  * up = up 
17:13 < Filip>  * down = down 
17:13 < Filip>  * right = right 
17:13 < Filip>  * left = left 
17:13 < Filip>  * 
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt + ok = space 
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt + esc = backspace 
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt + pwr = ctrl + c 
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt + up = next alpha numeric char 
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt + down = previous alpha numeric char 
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt + right = select current alpha numeric and move to next 
17:13 < Filip>  * rkt + left = overwrite previous alpha numeric char 
17:13 < Filip>  
17:14 < Baalz> This would be easier:
17:14 < Baalz> up = next alpha numeric char
17:15 < Baalz> down = previous alpha numeric char
17:15 < Baalz> rkt + up = up
17:15 < Baalz> rkt + down = down
17:15 < Baalz> You understand what I mean?
17:16 < Filip> yes, I  see. I think antagonizt made up the current mappings, but it's not hard to change them
17:18 < antagonizt> hey folks
17:19 < Baalz> Hi antagonizt
17:19 < Filip> that's the one
17:19 < Filip> h's guilty ;-)
17:19 < Baalz> :)
17:19 < antagonizt> I think the the driver should be much simpler and just return a masked byte with what is down...
17:19 < antagonizt> there should be a userland daemon process that interperts the buttons based on a config file
17:20 < antagonizt> a button keyboard daemon
17:21 < Filip> with a possibility to reconfigure on the fly
17:21 < antagonizt> i never thought the current driver was anything more than a stop-gap solution
17:21 < Baalz> Yeah but switching the effects of the buttons would make it much easier to input text for the moment
17:21 < Filip> have different mappings for different  applications
17:22 < someguy> any luck on locating the touchscreen stuff?
17:22 < antagonizt> although i'm not sure how to send keycodes form userland? maybe write them back to the driver?
17:22 < Filip> hi someguy
17:22 < someguy> hi
17:22 < antagonizt> we know where at least some of the touchscreen is... don't we?
17:22 < Filip> no, i've been looking at interrupts but haven't had a lot of time lately
17:23 < Filip> indeed, we know some locations,  but doesn't look like it's  sufficient to get x/y
17:24 < someguy> on the docs for the PIU on the other NEC chips, it looks like it uses multiple buffers for x/y data
17:24 < Filip> we can detect  pen up/down, but no position 
17:24 < someguy> and may need the driver to actually change the states on the PIU
17:24 < antagonizt> if it works anything like a mouse... which iirc it does... then there are no x/y coords to find
17:24 < antagonizt> just offsets from the last position
17:25 < Filip> it's different: mouse gives delta's (you can lift the mouse and place it elsewhere, cursor stays)
17:26 < Filip> touchscreen you can lift stylus, but when you touch again, that becomes the active point
17:27 < antagonizt> but that movement is equivelant to a mouse drag... no?
17:28 < someguy> on their other VR chips, they give location as AD Converter output
17:28 < someguy> then the driver converts that number to the location, based on calibration info
17:30 < someguy> I have to get going, will be back later - maybe my serial cable came in the mail
